'''Martin Kneser''' (21 January 1928 &ndash; 16 February 2004) was a German mathematician. His father [[Hellmuth Kneser]] and grandfather [[Adolf Kneser]] were also mathematicians.

He obtained his PhD in 1950 from the [[Humboldt University of Berlin]] with the dissertation ''"Über den Rand von Parallelkörpern''". His advisor was [[Erhard Schmidt]].

His name has been given to [[Kneser graph]]s which he studied in 1955. He also gave a simplified proof of the [[Fundamental theorem of algebra]].

Kneser was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] 1962 in Stockholm.<ref>{{cite book|year=1962|chapter=''Einfach zusammenhängende algebraische Gruppen in der Arithmetik'' by M. Kneser|title=Proc. Int. Congr. Stockholm|pages=260–263|chapter-url=http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1962.1/Main/icm1962.1.0260.0263.ocr.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171112073833/http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1962.1/Main/icm1962.1.0260.0263.ocr.pdf|archive-date=2017-11-12|url-status=dead}}</ref> His main publications were on [[quadratic forms]] and [[algebraic groups]].
